intro: How Machina was built, milestone by milestone. Each entry is what shipped and was committed that day, including what did not work.

entries.title: Foundation
items: Data-driven builders for fixed-wing aircraft, rotorcraft and tracked vehicles, with every part selectable
Explode view, deep links and generated airliners measured against their published size

entries.title: Original app design
items: The Hangar design system with dark, light and blueprint themes
Home page, category pages and gallery with 3D thumbnails, search and sort
Keyboard shortcuts, phone layout and accessibility work

entries.title: Real models
items: Open-licensed FlightGear aircraft loaded at runtime, with parts named from their meshes
Fifteen aircraft, X-ray view, a 1.8 m scale figure and a quality standard for listing a model
First parametric builder: a Boeing 737-300 lofted from published dimensions, then a Tu-154M measured from an open three-view drawing

entries.title: Drawings and generated detail
items: A3 three-view drawings projected from the 3D model as exact vectors, with sections, dimensions and a title block
Generated detail on parametric aircraft: panel seams, framed windows, control surface gaps, fan blades, gear linkage, antennas and beacons
Livery presets, then custom colors for any model whose livery can be recolored

entries.title: Mesh to parametric, and an accuracy benchmark
items: A converter that measures a detailed mesh into a parametric model with no per-model settings
A320neo, 787-8, 747-400 and 707 converted, scored 0.86 to 0.99 silhouette overlap against their source meshes
Light-aircraft rebuilds tried and kept unlisted: they came out worse than the originals

entries.title: Model page redesign
items: Livery palette in the viewer, a filterable parts rail with collapsed groups, and vertical tabs for overview, specs, drawing, sources and the selected part
Both side panels fold away as drawers to give the 3D view more room

entries.title: More aircraft, with their cockpits
items: Cockpits and cabins imported for the FlightGear aircraft, and simulator skins drawn on both sides so cabin walls show through the glass
Tupolev Tu-134A, Ilyushin Il-76TD and Concorde added, with airline titles and registrations painted out
Tu-154B-2, Tu-144D and Yak-40 kept unlisted: the Tupolevs store their landing gear folded and it could not yet be lowered correctly

entries.title: Validation gate
items: Every listed model must pass checks in the test suite: all wheels on the ground, no missing stretch along the length, nothing from the cabin outside the fuselage, and only textures a browser can load
Added after models were listed with floating gear, a missing nose cone and light-beam cones under the fuselage

entries.title: Public release
items: Open source at github.com/al-ex-ai/Machina and live at machina.al-ex.ai
A deploy is a git push: the server checks out the commit and stamps it onto every module URL, so Cloudflare serves fresh code

entries.title: Faster catalog
items: The catalog opens without the 3D engine: Three.js loads when a model page needs it, and in the background once the thumbnails are in
One catalog file instead of seventeen requests, preloaded with the page, and a year of caching for every commit-stamped file
A first visit went from about 3 seconds after the page arrived to about 0.4 seconds

entries.title: Compare
items: Line up two to four models on one apron, or stack the real aircraft on one spot, largest at the bottom, with the others taxiing in one by one, all at true scale
A three-view silhouette sheet at one scale and a spec table that shows how each model differs from the first
Line up every listed model, sorted by length, span, height, weight, speed or first flight
One screen with tabs for the line-up, overlay, silhouettes and specs, so nothing needs scrolling, and Machina's own dropdown in place of the browser's select
The first line-up used the three-quarter camera, which made the farthest airliner look as small as the nearest; it now faces the row nose on
The first overlay drew every model see-through, then in flat colors; both looked like toys, so it became the real aircraft with a wash of color and a taxi-in

entries.title: Real meshes only, and one standard for every model
items: The catalog holds real meshes only: the A380 from the Omega Hangar model, the 777 and the 707 from their full FlightGear packages, and the Tu-154M and DC-3 back in the workshop because they did not reach the bar
Helicopters get their own category; categories carry classes, and collections group models such as the true-scale line-up and Warbirds
A new home page built around "Machines, as they really are", with every listed model side by side at true scale
Warbirds: the Spitfire Mk IX and P-51D Mustang join the SR-71, each with its cockpit and its undercarriage down
Neutral liveries: registrations, flags and maker lettering painted out of the light aircraft and the EC130; the P-51D and 737 wear the Machina livery
A color picker on every detailed model, including camouflage, bare metal, black paint and fabric, leaving markings, tyres and wood alone
Every texture as WebP and capped at 2048 px: 96.5 MB of PNG down to 19.4 MB, each model under a 20 MB budget
Drawing sheets follow the standard three-view set, with wheelbase, track, tail span and a scale bar
National markings painted off the Spitfire and SR-71
Phone and tablet layouts: every page link and search reachable in a two-row header, and a true-scale line-up that keeps a readable scale and scrolls sideways on small screens
A written model standard (MODEL_STANDARD.md): 23 rules a model must pass before it is listed

entries.title: Faster X-ray and Compare, and two propliners
items: The Machina livery tried on every model, then kept only where it renders clean: A320neo, 787-8 and Ercoupe joined the list, and the An-225 and twelve others went back to their own paint because old cheatlines and titles showed through
X-ray outlines built in a background worker after the model loads, merged per part: on the 777 the switch went from 2.9 s to 0.2 s and from 8 to 41 fps
Compare merges each model by material and draws cabins only up close: four airliners went from 7,671 to 209 draw calls and from 12 to 55 fps, every model at once from 3 to 25 fps
Select a model in Compare with a click or tap to open it, see its specs or remove it; small aircraft stay easy to hit on a phone
A model opened from a scrolled page starts at the top
Junkers Ju 52/3m in silver duralumin, with the crosses and lettering painted off its tail

Lockheed L-1049H Super Constellation with the Eastern Air Lines livery painted off, in a new Propliners collection with the Ju 52; its three fins stand 8.47 m against the published 7.54 m, which the model notes
The gear tool mirrored two doors of one nacelle as if they were left and right twins, which left the Constellation's doors floating; it now mirrors only true pairs

entries.title: Takeoff
items: A takeoff scene for the Super Constellation: engine run-up, a 1,500 m roll, rotation at 112 kt, liftoff and climb out on a 3 km runway, at 1x, 2x or 4x
Gear, doors, oleos, flaps, elevator, propellers and wheels move by the model's own FlightGear animations, kept by the gear tool instead of frozen gear down
Follow, runway spotter and chase cameras; the spotter's lens zooms to keep the aircraft in frame
Animations now nest as FlightGear nests them, later ones inside earlier ones: the first try spun the wheel hubs about their static axle after the oleo had moved them, so they floated under the wing

The runway flickered: tiny edge lights and fine asphalt grain sparkled in motion, and the grass under the runway fought it for depth at a distance; lights gone, grain softened, grass cut around the runway, shadow box snapped to its texels

next: Takeoff for more aircraft, one at a time and only where the model's own animations hold up
Next real aircraft: Boeing 314 Clipper, DC-6, CH-47, Alouette III, Bell X-1, ATR 72 and EC135, each held to the model standard
M4 Deeper detail: labels and a measure tool, cutaway view
